result.title: Policy Invariance Is Not Learning Invariance: Potential-Based Reward Shaping for Navigation with a Limited View
result.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Under review at the MATH4AI Workshop at AAAI 2027
result.summary: Potential-based reward shaping (PBRS) does not change the optimal policy, but how much it speeds up learning depends on the potential and on effects outside this guarantee. We analyse how PBRS changes the one-step reward while it preserves the discounted return: a per-step $(γ-1)Φ$ term, the terminal-state rule, a constant shift of the potential, and positive cycles in a bonus that is not potential-based. We then measure these consequences in pre-registered experiments with a PPO agent. The agent has a limited egocentric view and is tested on two MiniGrid navigation tasks (160 runs, 10 seeds per condition). On LavaCrossing, a geodesic (BFS) potential learned faster than both the sparse baseline and a Euclidean potential with a 7x7 and a 5x5 view (AUC difference +0.27 to +0.39, Holm p between 0.007 and 0.0499). The Euclidean potential did not differ from the baseline. In 20 runs with a non-potential bonus, none of the agents learned the task. The Euclidean potential caused more than twice as many deaths in lava during early training. View size did not detectably change the benefit of shaping. With a 5x5 view on SimpleCrossing, some BFS runs got stuck in loops and never learned; shifting the potential did not remove this, so the per-step term alone does not explain it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析 potential-based reward shaping 在保持折扣回报不变的前提下如何改变单步奖励（如 (γ−1)Φ 项、终态规则、势函数平移与非法正环），并以预注册的 PPO 实验在带有限自视角的 MiniGrid 导航任务上测量其学习加速与副作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 「不改变最优解却改变学习过程」的奖励塑形分析，可能为 LVR 中轨迹监督、中间信号的贡献分配与训练设计提供类比线索；受限视角下的部分可观测导航也与证据获取相关，但距离视觉语言推理主线较远，需核查其可迁移性。
